_meta.purpose: Data source for the Study Budget Tracker widget. One object per deanery. The widget renders: brief + approval verdict + pre-drafted approval email. On the hub page the widget shows the deanery dropdown (defaultDeanery=null). On each deanery article the widget is pre-selected (defaultDeanery=<slug>) with emailOpen=true.
_meta.sourceLinksOutstanding: 13 deanery pages sourced. South West detailed funding position unconfirmed (regional links partly down); article treats a commercial SCA course as a possibility needing approval, not a certainty. East of England cites the live FAQ URL (2020 PDF bundled). North East cites a second bundled doc.

deaneries.name: London
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: Likely approved: one SCA preparation course up to £600, with ES agreement.
deaneries.brief: London funds one SCA preparation course up to £600 under code GP0001, with your Educational Supervisor's agreement. Online packages qualify. Question bank claims use up the same single course. Exam fees are not covered by the budget.
deaneries.sourceDoc: General Practice approved study leave list (Sept 2025) + NHS England London & South East GP exam preparation FAQ

deaneries.name: Kent, Surrey and Sussex
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: Likely approved: one SCA course per sitting, up to £600.
deaneries.brief: KSS funds one SCA preparation course per sitting up to £600 under code GP0001, an external supporting activity needing supervisor sign off. Free internal AKT revision (GP0017) is available separately. Exam fees are not covered.
deaneries.sourceDoc: KSS General Practice Approved List, revised March 2026

deaneries.name: East of England
deaneries.cap: No fixed allocation; TPD sign off for exam courses
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: Conditional: one SCA course per programme, TPD sign off, regional free courses come first, expensive commercial packages generally declined.
deaneries.brief: East of England has no fixed personal allocation. Exam preparation courses are aspirational activities needing TPD sign off and a PDP entry. Book the free regional SCA day first. Expensive commercial packages are generally not reimbursed except in exceptional circumstances.
deaneries.sourceDoc: NHSE East of England GP Study Leave FAQs (live) + TPD guidance Oct 2020 (bundled secondary)

deaneries.name: Thames Valley
deaneries.cap: No cash cap; one SCA course in ST3
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: Likely approved: SCA course in ST3 is a green curriculum requirement, ideally RCGP accredited. Regional courses come first.
deaneries.brief: Under the joint Thames Valley and Wessex policy an SCA course in ST3 is automatically fundable, one per resident doctor, ideally RCGP accredited. Book the regional course first. A subscription bundled inside a course fee is acceptable; a standalone subscription is not.
deaneries.sourceDoc: Study leave for GP resident doctors, Thames Valley and Wessex GP School, March 2026

deaneries.name: East Midlands
deaneries.cap: No per-course cap (extra approval above £1,000 total)
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: Likely approved: SCA courses are mandatory curriculum activity, ES sign off, guidance of two over training, no cap below £1,000.
deaneries.brief: Under the Midlands GP Schools guidance, SCA courses are Category I mandatory activity needing only ES approval, with guidance of two courses over training and RCGP-accredited preferred. No per-course cap; only claims over £1,000 total need extra TPD sign off. Online courses treated the same as in-person.
deaneries.sourceDoc: Midlands GP Schools Study Leave Guidance, current version May 2026

deaneries.name: North West
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: Conditional: one SCA course up to £500. RCGP-accredited courses are auto-approved; non-accredited need TPD and study-leave-team sign off before booking. Courses over £500 are not fully funded.
deaneries.brief: North West funds one SCA course up to £500. RCGP-provided or accredited courses are automatically approved; non-accredited courses are considered case by case, held to the same £500 line, and need TPD and study-leave-team sign off before booking. Fourteen Fish packages are funded separately. A £599 course sits £99 above the cap.
deaneries.sourceDoc: NW School Study Leave Guidelines, March 2026

deaneries.name: Yorkshire and Humber
deaneries.cap: No stated cash cap; named approved list
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: Likely approved: SCA courses are green (auto-approved on ALM), one per exam attempt, from a named list.
deaneries.brief: Yorkshire and Humber auto-approves SCA courses on ALM, one per exam attempt, from a named list (RCGP SCA course, SCA assured course, complete SCA course). Funding is provided if no free or pre-funded course is available. Confirm reimbursement permission before booking; 8 weeks' notice.
deaneries.sourceDoc: Study leave for GP Registrars, Yorkshire and Humber, February 2025

deaneries.name: North East
deaneries.cap: Full funding if RCGP accredited; else 50% self-funded
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: Conditional: one RCGP-provided or accredited SCA course or package is auto-approved with full funding. Non-accredited courses are discretionary with 50% self-funding expected.
deaneries.brief: North East auto-approves one RCGP-provided or accredited SCA course or educational package per trainee, with full funding. Non-accredited courses fall into the discretionary route where you pay 50% yourself. Subscriptions are not funded. Applications over £500 need extra sign off. Never pay before approval or the claim is auto-rejected.
deaneries.sourceDoc: NHSE Education NE Automatic Approved Course List, effective 05.09.2025 + NHSE NE Study Leave Policy v11, Aug 2025

deaneries.name: Scotland
deaneries.cap: £600 nominal per ST year (course fees, not subscriptions)
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: Conditional: a nominal £600 per ST year, TPD-judged on curriculum relevance and value. A course using most of the £600 may be part-funded only. No exam fee funding.
deaneries.brief: Scotland (NES) gives a nominal £600 per part of training, not automatic, requested with good reason via TURAS and approved by your TPD. Individual course fees are funded; annual subscriptions to a set of courses are not. Courses using most of your £600 may be part-funded. Exam fees are never funded.
deaneries.sourceDoc: NES GP registrar study leave FAQs, July 2025

deaneries.name: Wales
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: Likely approved: £600 per training year, rolling over once to £1,200 max. Curriculum-supplementing courses and even GP CPD subscriptions are acceptable.
deaneries.brief: Wales (HEIW) gives £600 per training year, with unused budget rolling over once to a £1,200 maximum for trainees staying in a Welsh programme. Curriculum-supplementing courses qualify, and Wales unusually lists GP CPD subscriptions as acceptable use. Exam fees, portfolio fees, books and equipment are excluded.
deaneries.sourceDoc: HEIW GP Trainee Study Leave Policy, V4, March 2024

deaneries.name: Northern Ireland
deaneries.cap: £750 per course via SUCCESS (after a failed attempt only)
deaneries.approvalLikelihood: After a failed attempt only: NIMDTA does not routinely fund SCA courses for a first sitting. After an unsuccessful attempt, SUCCESS funds one approved SCA course up to £750.
deaneries.brief: Northern Ireland (NIMDTA) does not routinely fund SCA courses for a first attempt, as protected self-directed learning time is the intended preparation. After an unsuccessful attempt, the SUCCESS programme funds one approved SCA course up to £750 (within a £1,250 per-year cap) plus up to 3 days study leave. Exam fees are never funded.
deaneries.sourceDoc: NIMDTA GP Specialty Training Study Leave guidance, October 2025
